_comment: The sweep we intend to run. This file is the EXPECTED state; results/ is the
observed state. Nothing else in the pipeline knows what a complete sweep is.
Two problems it exists to solve, both from benchmark/ci/AUTOMATION.md §4:
1. A cell that never reports publishes nothing and complains about nothing.
Absence is invisible on a dashboard that renders what exists, so a missing
cell is indistinguishable from one nobody asked for. Diff observed against
this to tell them apart.
2. A cell that reports n=10 against an expected count taken from its own job
input is self-certifying. The expected count has to come from here.
CORRECTED 2026-09-21 against the actual run data, having first been written
from memory. Three errors, and the pattern in all three is that a declared-truth
file written from recollection is worse than no file, because the gate that
reads it then produces confident wrong answers:
- qwen3.5-122b was omitted as 'retired', but it has 10/10 runs in seven
PUBLISHED cells. The gate would never have examined them -- a published
cell the gate cannot see is a hole in the only thing the gate is for.
- neurodesk-qwen3 was declared for 7t and motion and has never run there.
Permanent false 'missing cell' every time the audit runs.
- stroke was missing entirely despite 150 runs.
skills_hash per arm is the content hash the arm is DEFINED by. A run whose
recorded hash differs did not test the thing this arm claims to test, whatever
its directory was called. null means unchecked, not unimportant: env-only runs
record the hash of the snapshot that was present but not installed, which is
correct provenance and not something to assert on.

structural-brain-extraction-stroke: 150 runs exist on the VM and none are published. Its model and arm list
cannot be read from results/, so declaring it here would mean guessing --
which is exactly how the three errors above got in. Populate it from the
run data, not from memory: run assemble_audit once the stroke summary is
published, or read the cell list off ~/bench/runs.

_comment: Cells that can NEVER pass the 'no unresolved exclusions' gate, because the
runs needing re-run cannot be re-run. Recorded so the audit can separate
'nobody has got to this' from 'this is as good as it will ever get'.
These are not short on COUNT -- all are n=10. They are short on VALID runs:
some of the ten are excluded and the model that produced them is gone, so
the exclusion can never be resolved. A cell that will fail a gate forever
needs to be distinguishable from one that will pass once someone acts.
_known_permanently_short.reason: qwen3.5-122b was retired from the gateway in September 2026. 9 excluded runs (7 stroke, 2 nodura) can never be re-run.

neurodesk-qwen3: One run exists: structural-brain-extraction-7t-nodura | env+skill | n=1.
A model id that should not exist -- almost certainly a double-prefixed
`neurodesk/neurodesk-qwen3` from a mistyped dispatch. Deliberately NOT
declared as a model: declaring it creates a cell that can never be complete,
and not declaring it leaves one published run the gate never examines.
Neither is right, which is the point -- it is the same shape as the
truncated task id in INFRA_LEDGER entry 10, where fourteen graded outputs
belonged to nothing. Resolve by deciding whether that run is a qwen3 run
mislabelled, or junk to be removed.
